synopsis: Exhaustive field coverage of more than 7,000 testing strata is infeasible; the booklet therefore calls for stratified sampling plus simulation, with important machine, site and weather strata deliberately sampled and weighted back to operational prevalence [f132, f6829]. Coverage, failure discovery and performance estimation must remain separate: release-rate claims require a frozen, stratified random sample drawn from the declared operating-domain distribution before tuning and never used for tuning [f11334, f14131]. Random and probability-weighted sampling can support unbiased detection and false-alarm estimates with classical confidence intervals, but those claims fail if the assumed scenario distribution does not match real operation; defensible parameter distributions are an identified weak point, and the required field distribution is unavailable in public sources [f6830, f6833, f14086, f14132]. The booklet consequently urges shadow-mode logging on the existing warning fleet now, and requires acceptance criteria, strata, confidence levels and stopping rules to be fixed before hardware arrives [f14133, f14292]. A claim of at most 1% misses in each of 20 critical strata needs about 6,000 independent zero-miss trials; encounters, runs, shifts or sites—not individual frames—must determine the effective sampling units [f6887, f5462].
